summary: Comprehensive test suite for email/password login functionality covering successful authentication, edge cases, negative scenarios, and API-level validation. Focus areas include input validation, security controls, session management, and error handling.

happy_path.title: Successful login with valid email and password
preconditions: User has a registered account
User is on the login page
Account is active and not locked
steps: Enter a valid registered email address in the email field
Enter the correct password in the password field
happy_path.expected_result: User is authenticated successfully and redirected to their account dashboard/home page. A valid session is created.

happy_path.title: Successful login with email containing uppercase letters
preconditions: User has a registered account with a lowercase email
User is on the login page
steps: Enter the registered email address using mixed or uppercase letters (e.g., USER@EXAMPLE.COM)
happy_path.expected_result: User is authenticated successfully. Email comparison is case-insensitive.

happy_path.title: Successful login and session persistence across page refresh
preconditions: User has a registered account
User is on the login page
steps: After successful login, refresh the browser page
happy_path.expected_result: User remains logged in after page refresh. Session is maintained.

happy_path.title: Successful login redirects to originally requested page
preconditions: User is not logged in
User attempts to access a protected page directly
steps: Navigate directly to a protected URL
Get redirected to the login page
happy_path.expected_result: User is authenticated and redirected to the originally requested protected page.

happy_path.title: Successful login with Remember Me option
preconditions: User has a registered account
Login page has a Remember Me checkbox
steps: Close the browser and reopen it
happy_path.expected_result: User remains logged in after closing and reopening the browser. A persistent session cookie is set.

edge_cases.title: Login with email containing leading and trailing whitespace
preconditions: User has a registered account
User is on the login page
steps: Enter the registered email with leading and trailing spaces (e.g., '  user@example.com  ')
edge_cases.expected_result: System trims whitespace and authenticates the user successfully, or provides a clear validation error.

edge_cases.title: Login with very long valid email address
preconditions: A user account exists with a very long email (close to max allowed length)
User is on the login page
steps: Enter a valid email address at the maximum allowed character length
edge_cases.expected_result: User is authenticated successfully without any truncation or error.

edge_cases.title: Login with password containing special characters
preconditions: User account exists with a password containing special characters (e.g., !@#$%^&*())
User is on the login page
steps: Enter the password containing special characters
edge_cases.expected_result: User is authenticated successfully. Special characters in passwords are handled correctly.

edge_cases.title: Login attempt on an account that was just created
preconditions: User has just completed registration
Email verification is completed if required
steps: Navigate to the login page immediately after registration
Enter newly registered email and password
edge_cases.expected_result: Newly registered user can log in successfully without any delay or error.

edge_cases.title: Login with password containing Unicode or international characters
preconditions: User account exists with a password containing Unicode characters
User is on the login page
steps: Enter the password with Unicode characters (e.g., accented letters, CJK characters)
edge_cases.expected_result: System handles Unicode characters correctly and authenticates the user successfully.

edge_cases.title: Login with JavaScript disabled in the browser
preconditions: User has a registered account
JavaScript is disabled in the browser
steps: Disable JavaScript in the browser settings
edge_cases.expected_result: Login either works via server-side form submission or an appropriate message informs the user that JavaScript is required.

edge_cases.title: Simultaneous login from multiple devices
preconditions: User has a registered account
Two different devices or browsers are available
steps: Log in with valid credentials on Device 1
Log in with the same valid credentials on Device 2
edge_cases.expected_result: System either allows concurrent sessions per defined policy or invalidates the previous session with an appropriate notification.

negative_scenarios.title: Login with incorrect password
preconditions: User has a registered account
User is on the login page
steps: Enter a valid registered email address
negative_scenarios.expected_result: Login fails. A generic error message is displayed (e.g., 'Invalid email or password'). User is not authenticated.

negative_scenarios.title: Login with unregistered email address
preconditions: User is on the login page
steps: Enter an email address that does not exist in the system
negative_scenarios.expected_result: Login fails. A generic error message is displayed that does not reveal whether the email exists (e.g., 'Invalid email or password').

negative_scenarios.title: Login with empty email field
preconditions: User is on the login page
negative_scenarios.expected_result: Login is prevented. A validation error is displayed indicating that the email field is required.

negative_scenarios.title: Login with empty password field
preconditions: User is on the login page
steps: Enter a valid registered email address
negative_scenarios.expected_result: Login is prevented. A validation error is displayed indicating that the password field is required.

negative_scenarios.title: Login with both fields empty
preconditions: User is on the login page
steps: Leave both email and password fields empty
negative_scenarios.expected_result: Login is prevented. Validation errors are displayed for both fields.

negative_scenarios.title: Login with invalid email format
preconditions: User is on the login page
negative_scenarios.expected_result: Login is prevented. A validation error is displayed indicating the email format is invalid.

negative_scenarios.title: Account lockout after multiple failed login attempts
preconditions: User has a registered account
Account lockout policy is configured (e.g., 5 failed attempts)
steps: Enter the valid email with an incorrect password
Repeat step 2 until the maximum allowed failed attempts is reached
Attempt to log in one more time
negative_scenarios.expected_result: Account is locked after the threshold is reached. An appropriate message is displayed (e.g., 'Account locked. Please reset your password or try again later.').

negative_scenarios.title: Login attempt with a deactivated or suspended account
preconditions: A user account exists but has been deactivated or suspended by an admin
steps: Enter the email and correct password of the deactivated account
negative_scenarios.expected_result: Login fails. A message is displayed informing the user their account is deactivated/suspended with guidance on next steps.

negative_scenarios.title: Login attempt with an unverified email account
preconditions: User registered but has not verified their email address
steps: Enter the email and correct password of the unverified account
negative_scenarios.expected_result: Login fails or is restricted. User is prompted to verify their email address before accessing the account.

negative_scenarios.title: SQL injection attempt in email field
preconditions: User is on the login page
steps: Enter a SQL injection string in the email field (e.g., "' OR '1'='1'; --")
negative_scenarios.expected_result: Login fails. The system sanitizes the input and does not execute any injected SQL. No unauthorized access is granted.

negative_scenarios.title: XSS injection attempt in login fields
preconditions: User is on the login page
steps: Enter a script tag or XSS payload in the email field (e.g., "<script>alert('XSS')</script>")
negative_scenarios.expected_result: The input is sanitized and escaped. No script is executed. A validation error is displayed.

negative_scenarios.title: Login using a previously used expired session token
preconditions: User has a previously logged-in session that has expired
steps: Allow a user session to expire
Attempt to access a protected page using the expired session token
negative_scenarios.expected_result: Access is denied. User is redirected to the login page. Expired tokens are not accepted.

api_tests.title: POST /login returns 200 with valid credentials
preconditions: API endpoint is accessible
A valid user account exists
steps: Send a POST request to the /login endpoint
Include valid email and password in the request body as JSON: {"email": "user@example.com", "password": "validPassword123"}
api_tests.expected_result: Response status is 200 OK. Response body contains a valid authentication token (e.g., JWT) and user details. Token expiry is set appropriately.

api_tests.title: POST /login returns 401 with invalid credentials
preconditions: API endpoint is accessible
steps: Send a POST request to the /login endpoint
Include a valid email but incorrect password: {"email": "user@example.com", "password": "wrongPassword"}
api_tests.expected_result: Response status is 401 Unauthorized. Response body contains a generic error message. No token is returned.

api_tests.title: POST /login returns 400 with missing email field
preconditions: API endpoint is accessible
steps: Send a POST request to the /login endpoint
Omit the email field from the request body: {"password": "somePassword"}
api_tests.expected_result: Response status is 400 Bad Request. Response body contains a validation error specifying that email is required.

api_tests.title: POST /login returns 400 with missing password field
preconditions: API endpoint is accessible
steps: Send a POST request to the /login endpoint
Omit the password field from the request body: {"email": "user@example.com"}
api_tests.expected_result: Response status is 400 Bad Request. Response body contains a validation error specifying that password is required.

api_tests.title: POST /login returns 400 with invalid email format
preconditions: API endpoint is accessible
steps: Send a POST request to the /login endpoint
api_tests.expected_result: Response status is 400 Bad Request. Response body contains a validation error for invalid email format.

api_tests.title: POST /login rate limiting after repeated failed attempts
preconditions: API endpoint is accessible
Rate limiting is configured
steps: Send multiple POST requests to /login with invalid credentials in rapid succession
Exceed the configured rate limit threshold
api_tests.expected_result: Response status is 429 Too Many Requests after the threshold is exceeded. A Retry-After header may be included.

api_tests.title: POST /login response does not expose sensitive information
preconditions: API endpoint is accessible
steps: Send a POST request with invalid credentials
Inspect the response body and headers
api_tests.expected_result: Response does not reveal whether the email exists or specific reason for failure. No password hashes, internal stack traces, or sensitive server info are exposed.

api_tests.title: POST /login enforces HTTPS and rejects HTTP
preconditions: API endpoint is configured with HTTPS
steps: Send a POST request to the /login endpoint using HTTP (not HTTPS)
api_tests.expected_result: Request is either rejected or redirected to HTTPS. Credentials are never transmitted over unencrypted connections.

api_tests.title: POST /login returns valid JWT token structure
preconditions: API endpoint is accessible
A valid user account exists
System uses JWT
steps: Send a POST request to /login with valid credentials
Decode the returned JWT token and inspect its structure
api_tests.expected_result: JWT contains a valid header, payload, and signature. Payload includes user identifier, issued-at timestamp, and expiration time. Algorithm is secure (e.g., RS256 or HS256).

api_tests.title: POST /login with empty request body
preconditions: API endpoint is accessible
steps: Send a POST request to the /login endpoint with an empty JSON body: {}
api_tests.expected_result: Response status is 400 Bad Request. Validation errors are returned for both email and password fields.

api_tests.title: POST /login with Content-Type other than application/json
preconditions: API endpoint is accessible
steps: Send a POST request to /login with credentials as form-urlencoded or plain text instead of JSON
api_tests.expected_result: Response status is 415 Unsupported Media Type or 400 Bad Request with a clear error message if the endpoint only accepts JSON.

risk_areas: Security: Brute force and credential stuffing attacks — ensure account lockout and rate limiting are properly implemented
Security: SQL injection and XSS through login input fields — ensure all inputs are sanitized and parameterized queries are used
Security: Session management — ensure tokens are invalidated on logout, expiry is enforced, and sessions cannot be hijacked
Security: Sensitive data exposure — error messages must not reveal whether an email exists in the system (user enumeration)
Security: Transmission security — all credentials must be sent over HTTPS only; tokens must not appear in URLs or logs
Authentication: Password comparison — ensure passwords are hashed (e.g., bcrypt) and never stored or logged in plain text
UX: Clear and user-friendly error messages without compromising security details
Reliability: Login service availability and performance under high concurrent login loads
Integration: Token-based authentication compatibility with downstream services and APIs
Compliance: GDPR/privacy regulations around login attempt logging and failed authentication records
